title: Lisse finite direct image on a splitting cover
statement: Let $g:Z\to S$ be finite, $V$ an open of $S$, and $p:T\to V$ etale [def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions]. On $P=Z\times_S T$ [def-pc-fibre-product], with base map $q:T\to V\to S$, suppose finitely many pairwise disjoint opens $W_i$ cover $P$ and each $W_i\to P\to T$ is a universal homeomorphism [def-weil-universal-homeomorphism]. Let $E$ be an abelian etale sheaf on $Z$. If the underlying set sheaf of $E|_{g^{-1}(V)}$ is lisse [def-weil-pbc-etale-sheaves, def-weil-pbc-inverse-image], then $p^{-1}(V^{-1}(\operatorname{forget}(g_*E)))$ is lisse [def-weil-pbc-direct-image]. This is a statement on the cover $T$, with no descent or dense-open existence assertion.

proof.text: The first projection a:P to Z has image in g inverse image V by the pullback condition. Lift it through that open immersion to r:P to g inverse image V. Apply pullback_finite_locally_constant to r and the open inclusion, then rewrite their composite as a. This proves lissity of the underlying set sheaf of a inverse image E.

Apply the disjoint universal-homeomorphism local-constancy statement to the second projection b:P to T, the W_i, and a inverse image E. For finite geometric stalks, use the proved abelian finite-direct-image stalk formula. The forgetful functor commutes with stalks because it preserves filtered colimits, and with products because it preserves limits. The formula therefore identifies each underlying set stalk with a product of finite sets over the finite geometric fibre. Finite.of_equiv transfers finiteness to the direct-image stalk.

Choose the inverse-image/forgetful comparisons for V inclusion and p. Their inverse components identify the desired iterated set pullback with the underlying abelian iterated inverse image. The proved upperStarComp comparison identifies that with q inverse image of g direct image E. Apply finite base change for the pullback square of g and q, then forget abelian structure. Compose the isomorphisms. Finally transport local constancy by overPullback.mapIso and finite stalks by the geometric fiber functor applied to the inverse isomorphism.
